name: Ethics of AI
instructions:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming society at an unprecedented pace, influencing domains such as healthcare, finance, governance, and education. While AI offers immense opportunities, it also raises critical ethical concerns related to fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, and societal impact. This lecture introduces foundational concepts of AI ethics, tracing its origins from classical philosophy to modern computational systems. It explores key challenges such as algorithmic bias, data misuse, lack of explainability, and the unintended consequences of autonomous systems. The session highlights frameworks proposed by global organizations and illustrates ethical dilemmas through case studies. Students will engage in analysis and design exercises for responsible AI systems. The lecture concludes with a roadmap emphasizing the role of future data scientists in building trustworthy and human-centered AI systems.

Speaker: Prof. Partha Pratim Das
Professor, Department of Computer Science and Founding Director, Center for Data Science and Analytics, Ashoka University, Sonipat; (Formerly) Professor, Department of Computer Science & Engineering

Pre-requisites: No specific prerequisites-an open mind and curiosity about the limitations of AI are sufficient. However, experience with various uses of LLMs and ML models would help in better understanding. Knowledge of algorithms (and theory of computation) will further enhance comprehension in some parts.

name: Measurement of AI
instructions:
The rapid proliferation of Artificial Intelligence systems across domains has amplified the need for robust mechanisms to measure their performance, reliability, and societal impact. This lecture introduces foundational concepts, tracing the evolution from traditional evaluation metrics to modern frameworks for assessing complex AI systems, such as large language models and multimodal agents. It explores dimensions including accuracy, robustness, fairness, explainability, efficiency, and trustworthiness. The session highlights state-of-the-art techniques such as benchmark datasets, human-in-the-loop evaluation, and emerging metrics like BERTScore and GPTScore. Through examples and exercises, students examine limitations such as dataset bias and metric gaming and explore future directions in AI evaluation.

Speaker: Prof. Partha Pratim Das
Professor, Department of Computer Science and Founding Director, Center for Data Science and Analytics, Ashoka University, Sonipat; (Formerly) Professor, Department of Computer Science & Engineering

Pre-requisites: No specific prerequisites-an open mind and curiosity about the limitations of AI are sufficient. However, experience with various uses of LLMs and ML models would help in better understanding. Knowledge of algorithms (and theory of computation) will further enhance comprehension in some parts.

name: 8 Things You Wish You Had Known About LLMs
instructions:
LLMs have been the "in" thing in the world of AI of late. But, did you know that a typical company spends more than 2/3rd of its LLM-focused time in other activities not involving LLMs? In fact, a lot of time goes into making LLMs usable and useful. This effort spans critical problems related to managing and hosting the models, to making them perform well, and to serving them in reliable, secure ways without compromising on integrity. In this talk, you will hear about 8 broad problem areas that will need to be tackled in order to have an effective LLM-based / LLM-driven solution.

Speaker: Rangarajan Vasudevan
AI & Technology Advisor, Entrepreneur | Educator

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Beyond GPS: Wireless-Based Navigation and Imaging in Indoor Environments
instructions:
This workshop will explore how wireless signals can be harnessed for precise localization and environmental mapping in indoor spaces, where GPS signals are often unreliable or entirely unavailable. The session will be structured into two interconnected parts, blending theory with live demonstrations and interactive simulations to provide a hands-on learning experience.

Speaker: Prof. Ayon Chakraborty
Assistant Professor, Department of CSE, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Chart Deconstruction
instructions:
Deconstructing a chart amounts to a deeper version of the self-sufficiency test. It helps us understand what parts of the chart are doing what, and what cues certain parts send to readers. In better dataviz, every part of the chart is doing something useful, it is free of redundant parts that take up cognitive processing time for no reason, and the cues to readers move them towards the intended message, not away from it. In this workshop, you will learn how to break down a visualization into its core components - data, axes, legends, and visual mappings - to understand how it was built, evaluate its effectiveness, or reuse its structure. Through an hands-on exercise you will separate the visual representation (marks, colors, shapes) from the underlying data, understand the spatial relationships and constraints that hold the visual components together, and try to improve clarity through a redesign.

Speaker: Prof. Venkatesh Rajamanickam
Head - IDC School of Design, IIT Bombay

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Just bring a pen and paper for the hands-on activity.

name: The Economics of Pricing: How Firms Decide What to Charge
instructions:
Every product and service you use has a price that someone deliberately chose. But how? Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions a firm makes, yet it is rarely as simple as "cost plus margin." This workshop introduces the economic way of thinking through the lens of pricing strategy. Using a case inspired by a real-world scenario, participants will work through the questions a pricing team actually faces: what are customers willing to pay when you have data but not certainty, which costs should influence the price and which should be ignored, how do you price against a competitor who is watching and will respond, and when does it make sense to offer different prices to different customers? The goal is to equip participants with a practical framework for analysing pricing decisions and a sharper eye for the economic logic behind the prices they encounter every day.

Speaker: Dr. Bikramaditya Datta
Associate Professor - Dept of Economic Sciences, IIT Kanpur

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: From Messy to Smart: Build a File Organizer & Duplicate Cleaner with Python
instructions:
Tired of messy folders and wasting time searching for files?

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to automate everyday tasks using Python by building a smart application that organizes files and removes duplicates efficiently. This session focuses on real-world problem-solving, helping you transform your coding skills into practical solutions.

Speaker: Sivakoti Satyanarayana
Course Instructor (IITM BS Degree)

Pre-requisites: Basic knowledge of Python (variables, loops, functions); Laptop with Python installed; Interest in learning automation

name: Visual Intelligence: From Data to Interactive Dashboard
instructions:
Unlock the power of your data using Looker Studio. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to connect multiple data sources, design interactive dashboards, and transform raw data into meaningful insights. Explore dynamic visualizations, filters, and storytelling techniques to create impactful reports that drive smarter decisions.

Speaker: Atul Pratap Singh
Instructor (IITM BS Degree)

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds. Laptop required with good internet connection

name: Let AI Take Your Exams
instructions:
You've been told AI can pass your exams. But what happens when you actually watch it try - live, on your questions, in real time? This workshop starts with a collective experiment: we ask coding agents to solve real exams (including IITM exams) and see how it solves them. What follows isn't a tutorial on prompting - it's an autopsy that reveals what your exams are actually testing, where AI confidently hallucinates, and what that means for what's worth learning. You'll leave with a reframed understanding of your degree (the goal isn't answers, it's the ability to catch wrong ones) and a concrete study rituals that uses AI as a Socratic sparring partner rather than an answer machine. Come with a question you got wrong recently - it's going to be useful.

Speaker: Anand S
LLM Psychologist, TDS Faculty

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: AI in Healthcare: Opportunities
instructions:
Join us for an insightful workshop exploring the exciting intersection of AI and healthcare. Discover how AI is transforming the healthcare domain, from early disease detection to personalized treatments and beyond. Led by a cardiologist with a background in data science, machine learning, and AI, this workshop highlights the opportunities AI offers for medical research, diagnostics, patient care, and healthcare management. Ideal for working professionals and students from diverse fields aiming to pivot into healthcare or expand their knowledge.

Enhance your skill set and uncover new opportunities in this dynamic, evolving landscape. Don't miss this chance to learn and network!

Speaker: Ganesh Paramasivam
Professor and Head, Department of Cardiology, Kasturba Medical College, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal

Pre-requisites: None. If you are curious about this topic, join us!

name: Organic Learning
instructions:
The Need, Necessity & the Difficulty In today's environment, learning often becomes need-based—we study something only when required, solve what is immediately in front of us, and move on. While this works in the short term, it often leads to gaps in understanding and weak foundations over time. This workshop explores what it means to learn organically-in a way that builds depth, continuity, and real competence. We will work with examples taken directly from the B.S. program syllabus, looking at topics you are already familiar with, and examine how the same material can be approached either superficially or organically. Through these illustrations, we will see where learning can go off track and how consistency can change that trajectory. This will be a hands-on, discussion-driven session—no slides, no overload. The focus will be on thinking together, questioning habits, and exploring how to build a more meaningful approach to learning.

Speaker: Dr. Sudarshan Iyengar
IIT Ropar

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Staying Relevant in the Era of Job Cuts
instructions:
The skills that were valuable even a few years ago are rapidly changing. With the rise of AI and automation, simply knowing something is often not enough-what matters is whether what you know is still relevant. In this workshop, we will look at real examples and case studies to understand how the landscape is shifting: which skills are becoming less important, which ones are gaining importance, and why. The idea is not to create anxiety, but to build clarity on how one can stay relevant through continuous learning and thoughtful upskilling. The session will be interactive and example-driven, with no slides - just conversations, illustrations, and reflections. We will collectively think through what it means to stay updated and how each of you can align your learning with what the world increasingly demands.

Speaker: Dr. Sudarshan Iyengar
IIT Ropar

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Inside the Grey Box: A Peek into FPGA Accelerators
instructions:
This workshop introduces participants to digital hardware design on FPGAs, with an emphasis on building and testing a non-trivial design end-to-end. Using the PYNQ-Z2 platform, we will walk through the design of a simple image processing accelerator at both the register-transfer (RTL) and high-level synthesis (HLS) levels, and demonstrate how a working design is verified on hardware using an Integrated Logic Analyser (ILA). We will also show how such an accelerator can be accessed programmatically from Python, including through a browser-based interface.

Speaker: Prof. Nitin Chandrachoodan
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: Basic knowledge of digital systems (logic gates, flip-flops, FSMs) and working knowledge of Python and C. No prior HDL/FPGA experience required. RTL will be explained conceptually; demos will be shown live. It's open for both DS & ES Background

name: From Algorithms to Impact: AI-Powered Precision Health at Scale
instructions:
Health is inherently multidimensional and evolves uniquely for every individual. Yet, modern healthcare systems remain largely reactive-relying on late-stage detection, broad population-level interventions, and innovation models that are difficult to scale. Long drug development timelines, high clinical attrition rates, and steadily rising costs further constrain the timely delivery of effective care, particularly for populations bearing the highest disease burden. In this talk, I will discuss how the integration of scientific research with advances in AI and computing can help address these systemic challenges. I will present ongoing work towards building a unified AI-first framework that integrates multimodal sensing, advanced analytics, digital twins, and scalable computational platforms to enable precision health at population scale. Drawing on concrete examples from precision oncology, I will discuss how a sensing-to-modelling-to-action paradigm can support clinically meaningful decision-making - bridging data, clinical insight, and intervention - while maintaining scalability, and translational impact.

Speaker: Dr. Naveen Sivadasan
Principal Scientist, TCS Research

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: AI and the New Economics
instructions:
Who Creates Value, Who Reaps the Reward? AI is transforming how value is created—but the gains do not flow equally to everyone. This session explores how data, algorithms, platforms, and human judgment come together to create value, and why some firms, workers, and consumers capture much more of it than others.

The workshop examines the changing economics of competition, labor, and market power in an AI-driven world. For students who want to understand AI not just as a technology, but as a force reshaping the economy.

Speaker: Prof. Vimal Kumar
Professor, Department of Economic Sciences, IIT Kanpur

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Five Mistakes Data Scientists Make & How Economics Fixes Them
instructions:
Data science can build powerful models, but real-world decisions need more than prediction. This session looks at five common mistakes data scientists make—from mistaking correlation for causation to ignoring incentives, strategy, and the actual objective being optimized. Using clear examples and core economic ideas, the workshop shows how economics helps turn good models into better decisions.

For students who want to think beyond algorithms and understand how data-driven systems work in business, markets, and public policy.

Speaker: Prof. Vimal Kumar
Professor, Department of Economic Sciences, IIT Kanpur

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Creative Coding in JavaScript
instructions:
Increasingly powerful coding agents are gradually turning a section of coders into bystanders who review and accept AI generated code. The aim of this workshop is to reclaim human agency in a tiny but important way. Creative coding is a term that describes the process of using code as an artistic and design tool. Our goal is to rediscover the joy of coding with no AI assistance, focusing on the process of creation, rather than "getting things done quickly". By the end of this (anti-vibe-coding) workshop, you would have learnt to create simple animations yourself using JavaScript.

Speaker: Karthik Thiagarajan
Course Instructor (IITM BS Degree)

Pre-requisites: Good knowledge of at least one programming language. A basic knowledge of JavaScript is an added advantage.

A laptop is required. Students are expected to code along with the instructor during the workshop.

name: Building Interactive AI Applications: From Models to LLM-Powered Systems
instructions:
This hands-on workshop focuses on building interactive AI applications by progressively powering application interfaces with different types of models - from simple functions to machine learning models, transformer-based models through Huggingface, and through modern LLM APIs.

The workshop will cover:
• Designing interactive AI applications through rapid prototyping using Gradio
• Integrating classical ML models into applications
• Using transformer-based models for text generation via Huggingface
• Accessing large language models via modern APIs
• Quick deployment of the final application for external use using HF Spaces

Speaker: Dr. Anamika Chhabra
Lead DS/AI Instructor, IITM BS Program

Pre-requisites: Deep Learning, Bringing a laptop is preferred

name: Fundamentals of Secret Sharing
instructions:
This workshop introduces the fundamental ideas behind secret sharing—an important concept in modern cryptography where a secret is divided into multiple parts and distributed among participants, such that only authorized groups can reconstruct it. The session will build intuition through simple examples and progressively explore how such techniques are used to securely store and transmit sensitive information. Participants will also get a glimpse of how these ideas extend to visual data, such as images, highlighting practical applications in data protection and secure communication. The workshop includes short hands-on activities to help attendees understand the concepts through guided experimentation. No prior background in advanced cryptography is required, though basic familiarity with Python programming concepts will be helpful.

Speaker: Dr. Arup Kumar Chattopadhyay & Subendu Garai
Principal Project Officer, IITM BS Degree Programme; Teaching Fellow, IITM BS Degree Programme

Pre-requisites: Basic knowledge of Python, It is recommended to have a laptop.

name: Testing Big-Data Applications
instructions:
Big-data application development is moving heavily towards no-code/low-code development paradigms where data processing pipelines are developed for business intelligence without much coding background, mostly using proprietary tools. This session will outline the salient features of such platforms and also delve into testing such applications. We will highlight the important features to test big-data applications and also discuss some state-of-the-art techniques.

Speaker: Prof. Meenakshi D'Souza & Dr. Arup Kumar Chattopadhyay
Professor, HOD - CSE, IIIT-Bangalore; Principal Project Officer, IITM BS Degree Programme

Pre-requisites: Software Testing and Big-data courses, Java Programming, Laptop required

name: Building, Training and Testing Neural Networks with PyTorch
instructions:
This is a hands-on workshop designed to introduce participants to modern deep learning workflows using PyTorch. The workshop covers the complete lifecycle of neural network development: designing architectures, preparing datasets, training models, evaluating performance, and debugging learning behavior. Participants will gain practical experience implementing neural networks for classification and prediction tasks while understanding core concepts such as backpropagation, optimization, and model evaluation.

Speaker: Lakshmi Narasimhan
Associate Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: Basic Python programming skills and familiarity with PyTorch library. Laptop required

name: A Quick Tour of Logic in Computer Science
instructions:
The ability to model the world around us and reason with what we know is a hallmark of intelligence. Humankind has studied logic and reasoning since ancient times, both in Greece and in India. The goal has been to study valid arguments based on which truth values of (query) sentences can be determined. Computer scientists and mathematicians have sought to impart logical reasoning to machines.

We explore some of the logics that have been developed for machines, and look at the techniques that have been developed to arrive at the truth values of sentences. We begin with simple logics, and move on to more expressive languages. As we do so, we observe that reasoning becomes more computationally complex.

Speaker: Deepak Khemani
Professor - Plaksha University; Professor (adjunct), IIT Ropar; Former Professor - IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Setting Strategic Goals for AI-Driven Enterprises
instructions:
Enterprises accelerating AI adoption must define clear AI strategy goals to drive meaningful and scalable outcomes. A well-aligned approach ensures high-quality data, improves AI effectiveness, and directly supports business objectives while avoiding fragmented initiatives.
Evaluating enterprise readiness for AI initiatives
• Identifying high-value AI use cases aligned to business priorities
• Embedding AI into enterprise workflows and decision-making processes
• Defining data goals aligned with business and AI priorities
• Establishing data governance, quality, and consistency frameworks
• Enabling seamless data integration across systems and sources
• Building scalable data architecture to support AI workloads
• Ensuring data security, privacy, and regulatory compliance
• Resources and options to build AI talent required in modern enterprise

Speaker: Ravi Pandikunta
VP, Global Delivery Head, Data Analytics | AI, Tech Mahindra Limited

Pre-requisites: Brief idea on AI use cases and how it helps enterprises to drive efficiency and innovation. What are the tools/technologies available today to achieve this.

name: Introduction to NetworkX (Hands-on)
instructions:
This beginner-friendly session will introduce learners to the Python package-NetworkX-and will cover the following:
1. Creating and visualising directed and undirected graphs
2. Working with a real-life dataset (Zachary's Karate Club) and discerning interesting patterns by applying centrality measures and community detection approaches.

Speaker: Prof. Karthik Raman, Sandhya Vasudevan & Dipak Kanzariya
Professor, IIT Madras; PhD student; M.S student

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds. Laptops will be required as this will be a hands-on session

name: Dream to Frame
instructions:
A hands-on workshop exploring how AI can transform a simple idea into cinematic visuals, storyboards, and animated pre-visualizations. Participants will learn modern AI workflows used in filmmaking for concept development, shot design, visual storytelling, and virtual cinematography.

Speaker: Shashwat Mookherjee
CEO, Indierise Research Labs Pvt. Ltd

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all creative minds. Yes, a laptop is necessary. Additionally during the workshop, demonstrations will use paid tools; however, free alternatives will also be shown or shared.

name: The Motion Lab
instructions:
A practical workshop on AI-powered motion transfer, character animation, and cinematic performance generation. Participants will experiment with motion-driven visuals, talking portraits, AI actors, and expressive animation workflows used in next-generation filmmaking and digital storytelling.

Speaker: Shashwat Mookherjee
CEO, Indierise Research Labs Pvt. Ltd

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all creative minds. Yes, a laptop is necessary. Additionally during the workshop, demonstrations will use paid tools; however, free alternatives will also be shown or shared.

name: AI-Driven Telecom Analytics: Revenue Assurance & Fraud Management Use Cases
instructions:
This session will provide students with a practical introduction to Telecom Analytics, focusing on how AI, Big Data technologies, and investigative analytics are used in Revenue Assurance & Fraud Management (RAFM). The session will explore real-world telecom use cases involving fraud detection, revenue leakage identification, anomaly detection, and large-scale data processing across telecom B/OSS systems. Participants will gain insight into how finance, audit, operations, and technology converge in modern telecom analytics environments, along with an overview of AI-driven approaches used for operational intelligence and risk mitigation

Speaker: Daniel Peter
VP, Gamma Analytics

Pre-requisites: No prior telecom knowledge is required. The session is open to all students with an interest in AI, data analytics, technology, and real-world industry application

name: Small Language Models
instructions:
Small Language Models (SLMs) represent a shift in machine intelligence. Unlike Large Language Models (LLMs), SLMs are compact architecture. The number of parameters range from 100 million to 10 billion parameters. These models enable high-performance AI on resource-constrained hardware, including mobile phones, laptops, and edge devices.

We will examine SLM internal architectures, dive into specific optimization workflows, and evaluate practical deployment strategies for modern engineering environments.

Speaker: Prof. Ramaseshan Ramachandran
Visiting Professor, CMI

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Create a ChatGPT for your Files
instructions:
This hands-on workshop will teach participants how to build an AI assistant that can understand and answer questions from PDFs, images, documents, and other unstructured files using modern multimodal AI techniques. Participants will build a working prototype that can chat with uploaded files.

Speaker: Jimmi Kr. Bharti
Course Instructor (IITM BS Degree)

Pre-requisites: Basic Python programming knowledge & Familiarity with foundational AI concepts and LLMs (e.g., RAG, ChatGPT, OpenAI API) is helpful. Laptop required

name: How do Citizen Scale Apps like UPI and E-Commerce Handle Millions of Transactions Reliably Every Day?
instructions:
From UPI payments and online banking to food delivery and streaming platforms, there is a world of complex technology systems working behind the scenes. But when these systems slow down, fail, or behave unexpectedly, organizations need a way to quickly understand what went wrong and how it impacts users and businesses.

This is where system resilience becomes important. System Reliability and Operational Resilience is one of the fastest-growing areas in modern technology, helping organizations monitor, analyze, and improve the performance of large-scale digital systems in real time. As enterprises become increasingly digital and AI-driven, the demand for skilled professionals in SRE, IT Operations, and Reliability Engineering continues to grow rapidly.

This session will introduce you to the world of Observability - its scale, relevance, career opportunities, and the critical role it plays in powering the modern digital world.

Speaker: Rao Haridasu
Chief of Staff and Business Strategy, VuNet Systems

Pre-requisites: Some understanding of the layers of IT architecture would be helpful.

name: Context is the New Compute: Engineering Retrieval Systems That Actually Work in Production
instructions:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the default architecture for grounding LLMs in real-world data, but most production deployments still struggle with relevance, hallucinations, and scale.

This session moves past the textbook RAG pipeline and into what we've actually learned building Synapt.AI for Fortune 500 enterprises: how to design context layers that combine vector search, knowledge graphs, and structured retrieval; how to evaluate retrieval quality rigorously; and where AI agents break down when context engineering is treated as an afterthought.

Participants will leave with a clearer mental model of the modern RAG stack, the trade-offs between different architectural choices, and a sense of where the field is heading next

Speaker: Balasubramanian Chandran
Product & Engineering Leader, Prodapt

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: From Syntax to Sentience: A Journey from Classical NLP to Large Language Models (LLMs)
instructions:
This intensive workshop traces the evolution of Natural Language Processing. We begin with the fundamentals of text processing and linguistic foundations, move through the revolutionary "Attention" mechanism, and culminate in the architecture and fine-tuning of state-of-the-art Large Language Models. Participants will gain a conceptual and practical understanding of how machines learned to understand, generate, and reason with human language.

Speaker: Manojkumar Khara
Course Instructor IITM BS

Pre-requisites: Basic proficiency in Python programming - Foundational understanding of Linear Algebra and Probability. - Familiarity with Machine Learning basics (Supervised vs. Unsupervised learning) is recommended but not mandatory. Laptop required

name: Verification of Software
instructions:
We have all suffered the frustration of using buggy software. Can we automatically check whether a program works correctly? Alan Turing's foundational work on computability showed that this is impossible, in general. Nevertheless, there has been a lot of progress in building automated frameworks for checking correctness of different subclasses of programs. We explain some of the ingredients that go into building such formal verification systems and demonstrate some examples in a state-of-the art tool.

Speaker: Prof. Madhavan Mukund
Director, Chennai Mathematical Institute (CMI)

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Tell Me the Odds: Communicating Risk Numbers
instructions:
In this session we will focus on how risk is quoted and communicated. Often times, risk is mis-understood (even by students of statistics). That leads to wrong decisions. The session will provide case studies from various scenarios where risk numbers are important and often mis-communicated. Better mechanisms of talking about risk will be discussed. Risk-aware decision making will be discussed.

Speaker: Prof. Rahul R Marathe
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Bridging the DS/ES - A Glimpse into the World of Cyber-Physical Systems
instructions:
Cyber-physical systems (CPS) bridging the world of physical systems (electronic sciences) and cyber systems (data sciences) are increasingly becoming dominant in our everyday life e.g. AR/VR, automated driving, gesture recognition, structural health monitoring, perimeter sensing etc. In this workshop, we aim to offer a glimpse into cyber-physical systems through an unique example - distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) that transforms telecom fibers into dense sensor arrays for vibration and acoustic detection. Participants will explore foundational electronics like coherent interferometry, hands-on data processing pipelines for anomaly detection in infrastructure or security, and CPS integrations such as edge AI for predictive maintenance. Interactive demos and discussions will highlight challenges like signal denoising and scalability, empowering engineers to innovate in smart cities, energy grids, and beyond.

Speaker: Prof. Balaji Srinivasan
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: Students at or above the diploma level are preferred.

name: Cybersecurity in Embedded Devices
instructions:
Embedded devices are becoming an essential part of modern life, powering applications ranging from smart homes and industrial systems to healthcare and transportation. As these devices become more connected, ensuring their security has become increasingly important. This talk provides an overview of cybersecurity challenges in embedded systems, with a focus on both hardware security and firmware security. It will introduce common threats affecting embedded devices, discuss how vulnerabilities can arise at different layers of the system, and highlight the importance of designing security into devices from the beginning. The session will also explore general approaches used to protect embedded platforms, including secure hardware features, trusted firmware mechanisms, and secure update practices. Through examples from real-world applications, the talk aims to give attendees a broad understanding of the evolving embedded security landscape and the need for a holistic approach to device protection.

Speaker: Prof. Chester Rebeiro
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Representation Learning in Biology: Biomolecular Embeddings and Their Applications
instructions:
Can machines learn meaningful representations of biological systems? From classical k-mer counting to modern foundation models, we can now transform biological entities-such as DNA sequences, proteins, mutations, and disease states-into numerical vector representations known as embeddings. These embeddings capture rich biological patterns, enabling downstream tasks like protein function prediction and disease biomarker discovery. In this workshop, we invite students to explore the foundations of representation learning, and gain hands-on experience on extracting and applying biological embeddings (based on simple methods to state-of-the-art models like ESM and DNABERT).

Speaker: Prof. Manikandan Narayanan & Saish Jaiswal
Associate Professor, IIT Madras; PHD Researcher, IITM

Pre-requisites: Introductory linear algebra (vectors and similarity between vectors) and introductory machine learning concepts preferred for the lecture component. Basic knowledge of Python and a laptop required for the practical coding component. No prior biology knowledge is required-just an interest in how machines represent the language of life in a vector space! Laptop Required

name: What is Randomness?
instructions:
We explore the nature of randomness and its implications in mathematics, computer science, physics, and philosophy through discussions and interactive activities.

Speaker: Prof. Amritanshu Prasad & Prof. Sankaran Viswanath
Director, IMSc; Professor, IMSC

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Optimisation in Machine Learning
instructions:
Optimising over high dimensional continuous variables is challenging, important and has made significant advances in the last few years. We will go over the broad paradigms of this - constrained/unconstrained problems, and zeroth/first/second order methods. In particular several exciting new modifications of the vanilla first order gradient methods have unlocked new abilities – training multi-billion parameter models to a low loss on petabytes of data. We will go over some of those in this session. Mainly, we will look at gradient descent with momentum, adaptive gradient descent and MuON. We will see how a strong understanding of linear algebra and probability fundamentals makes the design of such novel algorithms possible.

Speaker: Harish Guruprasad Ramaswamy
Assistant professor, DSAI, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: ML Foundations (required), Deep learning (Nice to have), Machine learning

name: Build Your Own Mini Docker: Understanding Containers from Scratch
instructions:
Containers aren't magic they're clever Linux. In this 120-minute workshop, you'll build a working container from scratch in ~100 lines of code, learning exactly how Linux isolates processes, filesystems, networks, and users at the kernel level. You'll see the seven mechanisms that underpin all containerization and understand why they work the way they do. By the end, you won't just know what containers are you'll understand the fundamental Linux internals that make them possible.

Speaker: Sayan Ghosh
Software Engineer at SEEK, Course Instructor IITM BS

name: Back to Basics: Build Your Own LLM from Scratch
instructions:
Open the black box by building it yourself, from tokenizer to transformer, every layer, every weight, every line of code.

Speaker: Thejesh G N
Software Consultant, IITM BS Degree

name: Beyond Next-Token Prediction in Multimodal AI Models: Concepts, Reasoning, and Logic
instructions:
Modern AI systems excel at prediction - generating text, recognizing images, and solving increasingly complex tasks. Yet they still hallucinate, struggle with abstraction, and often fail at reliable reasoning. This raises a fundamental question: is intelligence simply prediction at scale, or does it require richer internal structure? In this talk, I will discuss our recent work studying the limits of multimodal LLMs – through new benchmarks and analyses, we show that state-of-the-art multimodal models still struggle with visual abstraction, spatial reasoning, and mental simulation, and that chain-of-thought prompting can sometimes even degrade performance. These findings suggest that fluent explanations may not necessarily reflect genuine reasoning. The second part will cover our recent work on concept-based learning, interpretable neural representations, semantic grounding, differentiable logic, and hierarchical abstractions in deep networks. Our observations herein motivate a broader research direction aimed at moving AI beyond opaque prediction toward concepts, structure, logic and compositional reasoning, with the broader goal of building models that are not only capable, but also reliable, interpretable, and trustworthy.

Speaker: Vineeth N Balasubramanian
Microsoft Research India and IIT-Hyderabad

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Compassion-A-Thon 3.0 From Idea to MVP to Incubation
instructions:
What separates a great idea from a funded startup? Execution - and knowing exactly where to start. In this workshop, Prof. Bala Ramadurai will walk you through the entire innovation journey that sits at the heart of Compassion-A-Thon 3.0 - from spotting a real, socially meaningful problem, to designing a solution, to building your first MVP, to walking into an incubation room with confidence. This is not a lecture. It is a masterclass in venture thinking. Dr. Bala will unpack how to validate whether your idea actually solves a problem people care about, how to structure your solution into a business model that holds up under scrutiny, and how pre-incubation pathways like Nirmaan IIT Madras work in practice. Drawing from his experience as a startup founder, IIT professor, GE research scientist, and Design Thinking expert, he will share frameworks, real startup stories, and hard-earned lessons that no textbook covers. You will leave understanding how Compassion-A-Thon's venture-first philosophy differs from a typical hackathon - and more importantly, what it takes to build something that is not just innovative, but impactful, scalable, and incubation-ready.

Speaker: Bala Ramadurai
International visiting Professor, Universidad Panamericana, Mexico, IITM-BS Degree Program, and NPTEL

Pre-requisites: Curiosity about solving real-world problems is all you need. Familiarity with Design Thinking or Lean Startup concepts is a plus - but not required. Open to all disciplines; interdisciplinary teams strongly encouraged. Laptop required.

name: Informed Career Decisions
instructions:
Career decisions are among the most consequential choices we make, yet they are often made with incomplete information and under social pressure. This session explores how to approach career choices more deliberately - understanding your own strengths and motivations, evaluating opportunities realistically, and recognising the trade-offs involved. The discussion will draw on real examples and encourage participants to think about long-term direction rather than short-term optimisation.

Speaker: Prof. Mahesh Panchagnula
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Data Science with Coding Agents
instructions:
Data-focussed, private, and lightning-fast—Small Language Models are redefining practical AI deployment. Join this 2-hour masterclass tailored for the IIT Madras Online BSc community to learn how to architect, train, and optimize your own SLM. Move past the hype of giant LLMs and discover how to build high-performance, cost-effective language models designed to run locally. Turn your foundational programming and data science skills into cutting-edge AI engineering.

Key Highlights / What You Will Learn:
The Case for SLMs: Why edge AI, privacy, and infrastructure costs are driving the industry toward smaller, hyper-focused models. Architectural Foundations: Compact transformer mechanics, tokenization, and vocabulary design. Training & Fine-Tuning Pipelines: Step-by-step walkthrough of dataset curation and optimization loops for limited compute.

Local Deployment: Strategies for running models efficiently on-device (browser/edge).

Speaker: Ashish Tendulkar
AI Practice Manager, Google

name: Optimization Models for Management Decisions
instructions:
Vipin B is an assistant professor in the Department of Management Studies at IIT Madras. Before joining IIT Madras, he was an assistant professor in the Department of Management Sciences at IIT Kanpur. Vipin received his PhD from IIT Madras in 2017. He is a recipient of DAAD fellowship. Vipin is a coordinator for the BS in Management and Data Science program offered by IIT Madras. He has published his research findings in leading management journals including Financial Times 50 (FT50) listed journal.

Speaker: Vipin B
Asst. Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Laptop with Microsoft Excel

name: Digital Twin for Mobility
instructions:
Mobility of passengers and goods is the backbone of a nation's economy. Safe, efficient, and sustainable mobility requires optimal planning and operations of the transport infrastructure. Digital twins of the mobility system enable decision makers make such optimal decisions through data driven, AI-augmented modeling and simulation. This workshop provides an overview on this emerging technology and how it impacts our mobility decisions.

Speaker: Prof. Gitakrishnan R
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required.

name: Sports Analytics & AI Workshop
instructions:
The Sports Analytics & AI Workshop is a one-hour interactive session designed for BS Data Science students at Indian Institute of Technology Madras to introduce the rapidly growing intersection of sports, artificial intelligence, and data science. The workshop aims to provide students with an overview of how modern AI technologies are transforming athletic performance analysis, injury prevention, strategy optimization, and sports training methodologies across various sporting disciplines. The session will explore the role of data-driven decision-making in sports and demonstrate how technologies such as Computer Vision, Machine Learning, IoT sensors, and real-time analytics are being applied in real-world sports environments. Students will gain insights into the development of intelligent systems capable of tracking athlete movements, analyzing biomechanics, monitoring performance metrics, and generating actionable feedback for coaches and athletes. The workshop will showcase several cutting-edge sports analytics solutions developed using AI-based approaches, including gait analysis through smart insoles, boxing movement analytics, racket sports tracking, cricket performance monitoring, swimming posture analysis, and markerless motion capture systems for weightlifting. These examples will help students understand how concepts from data science and AI can be translated into impactful applications within sports engineering and human performance optimization. In addition to technical demonstrations, the workshop will discuss the complete AI pipeline involved in sports analytics systems, including data acquisition, video processing, pose estimation, object tracking, feature extraction, predictive modeling, and visualization of insights. Students will also be introduced to emerging trends such as real-time sports intelligence, wearable analytics, automated video segmentation, and AI-assisted coaching systems. The primary objective of the workshop is to inspire students to explore interdisciplinary applications of data science beyond traditional domains and encourage innovation in AI-driven sports technologies. By the end of the session, participants will gain a foundational understanding of how AI and analytics are reshaping the future of sports and how their data science skills can contribute to this evolving field.

Speaker: Babji Srinivasan
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required.

name: Playing with AI - Autonomous Agentic Systems 101
instructions:
We all know AI is powerful - but often feel like AI systems can be unpredictable, or unreliable in real world scenarios and is better used for boilerplating / a google search alternative, and struggle to have confidence that our AI generated code or AI performed tasks - are bug/mistake free. This workshop will cover the basics of how we can reduce the amount of work that we need to do in order to have that confidence, and build clean, reliable systems that leverage both AI and traditional code - to (almost) fully autonomously perform tasks and build production grade code.

Speaker: Rishav Thakker
software architect and developer

Pre-requisites: Advanced computer usage required (being able to install and configure new software, good web search skills); Experience in using AI systems for work - at any level (chatgpt, claude, claude code); Basic coding knowledge preferred but not required; Strong software engineering fundamentals preferred but not required; Laptop required

name: Simulations for Bharat: AI for the Next Generation of Indian Engineering
instructions:
Simulations are the invisible workhorse of every single technological frontier today – From making GPUs to space exploration. In this workshop we will give an introduction to the simulation ideas powering our nations' aerospace, automotive, and defence revolution. We will see physical reality is captured in partial differential equations and simulated conventionally. We will also see how techniques in AI can be used to accelerate these solutions and how they could enable Bharat to develop a completely indigenous simulation stack.

Speaker: Balaji Srinivasan
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: Basic familiarity with Machine Learning, Neural networks. Comfort with calculus. Some exposure to NumPy/PyTorch or similar

name: Computing with Quantum Bits - A Curtain Raiser
instructions:
In this talk, we will introduce the quantum bit and give an overview of the scope and potential of quantum computing. We will also discuss the challenges that lie ahead, in scaling up from the noisy quantum processors of today to reliable, fault-tolerant quantum computers. We will conclude with a hands-on demonstration of implementing a quantum algorithm on present day quantum hardware.

Speaker: Prof. Prabha Mandyam
Professor, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required.

name: Digital Design for Testability
instructions:
India is positioning itself as a global player in the area of semiconductors. This is creating a demand for engineers skilled in design, manufacturing, assembly and testing of integrated circuits. Post-manufacturing testing is essential to eliminate defective chips and maintain quality. To improve the defect coverage and reduce the cost of testing, it is essential to include some test circuitry on the chip. Scan testing is a popular test mechanism in the industry to improve the testability of integrated circuits. Logic Built-in Self-Test (BIST) is used to reduce the dependence on expensive testers and allow in-field testing. In this half-day workshop, you will learn about testing of integrated circuits. Topics we will cover include
• Defects, Faults and Failures
• Combinational Testing
• Sequential Testing
• Scan Design
• Logic BIST
We will use a hands-on approach to make the course interesting. Students who have a background in Digital Design and Verilog HDL will benefit most from the course. You will gain insights about the semiconductor industry and learn the use of GenAI in automation.

Speaker: Dr. C.P. Ravikumar
Chief Learning Officer, VINYANA TECH

Pre-requisites: Laptop Required

name: Semiconductors: History and its Relevance in Modern World
instructions:
It has been said that semiconductors are for the information society, what grain was for the agrarian society and iron and steel were for the industrial society. Though semiconductor devices are some of the most abundant man-made objects on planet earth, we have realized their ubiquitous presence and importance only when there was a recent semiconductor shortage. Semiconductors are the most value added components of modern electronics. They enable all important functions like compute, connectivity, sensing and display. In this talk, I will give a short survey about the modern semiconductor industry, its history and how semiconductors are relevant to the modern world. The talk will be followed by a Q & A.

Speaker: Deleep R Nair
Professor Dept of EE, IIT Madras

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Electric Vehicles
instructions:
A basic overview of the different types of electric vehicles and the role of power electronics as an enabler of the EV revolution.

Speaker: Prof. L Umanand
Professor, IISc Bangalore

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.

name: Why Most AI Systems Fail and How to Build Ones That Don't
instructions:
A deep dive into why many AI systems that look impressive in demos fail in real-world scenarios. This session explores the hidden challenges behind building reliable AI, and introduces a new way of thinking about designing systems that move beyond simple retrieval to true understanding.

Speaker: Sheri Chander
AI Engineering Head, Newgen Software

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required.

name: From Assembly Line to Real Life: Testing What Ships
instructions:
What does it really take for a product to leave the factory and perform flawlessly in the hands of a customer? This talk explores the critical, often overlooked stage where engineering intent meets manufacturing reality-production-line testing. At scale, every unit must prove itself-not in controlled lab conditions, but on the line, within the constraints of time, variability, and throughput that define real-world production. Modern consumer products are increasingly complex, combining hardware, firmware, connectivity, and user experience into tightly integrated systems. Ensuring that each unit delivers consistently requires intelligent, fast, and repeatable validation embedded directly into the production process. This is where design-for-test meets manufacturing discipline-turning quality from an aspiration into a measurable, enforceable outcome. This session unpacks how organizations bridge the gap between design ambition and shipped reality, building test systems that scale without compromising rigor. It looks at how production-line validation becomes the final gatekeeper of user experience-quietly ensuring reliability, safety, and performance before a product ever reaches the customer. Because in the end, "what ships" isn't just hardware-it's trust, consistency, and confidence in every unit.

Speaker: Sundararajan Krishnan (PK)
Founder and CEO, BluArmor

name: From Chatbots to Autonomous Agents - The Next Operating System of Work
instructions:
AI is moving beyond chatbots into autonomous agents that can plan, decide, and act across real business systems. This session explores how agentic AI is becoming the next operating system of work — coordinating tools, data, and people to complete end-to-end tasks rather than answering isolated questions. We look at what changes when software stops waiting for instructions and starts pursuing goals, and what that means for how work is organised.

Speaker: Shabareesh Raj
Co-Founder & Chief AI Officer, sash.ai

Pre-requisites: No prerequisites required. Open to all curious minds.
